moves.evidence: LOW CONFIDENCE: MP calls Le Gringalet the ice line of the Mont Pinacle outcrop (east of Lac Lyster); leaf coordinate 45.02477,-71.89884 is within ~20 m of Mur de Zola 45.02497,-71.89891; no source names the wall

evidence: MP Mont Pinacle Ice page gives the single ice line Le Gringalet at 45.02477,-71.89884, essentially on top of the Mur de Zola pin. Placement rests on coordinates only; review.

A 2013 trip report (alavigne.net/Outdoors/ImageGallery/2013/03-29-Heffalump) puts The Heffalump on the Eardley Escarpment at the SW edge of Gatineau Park; Gripped also lists it as a west-end Ottawa-area flow. Leaf coordinate (45.957,-76.193) is far from the escarpment (~45.5N), so the pin should be reviewed.

MP lists Petit King as an ice climb on Mont-King (mountainproject.com/area/202282070/mont-king); Mini King not found online but name and grade pair with it. No wall name for the flows was found, so the leaf takes the route-derived name; LOW CONFIDENCE.

UNRESOLVED: MP Weir Ice Climbs page confirms Gros bras (WI4-5) at Weir; Marionnetiste, Le Fou du Roi, Petit bras and the M8 could not be placed on any named wall. All five stay together; a human should name the cliff (current name contains a discipline word).

MP Alsek Valley Ice: only one ice route established; access is the end of Alsek Valley Road, with the climb across the Dezadeash River (mountainproject.com/area/125746353). Name is descriptive, not a sourced wall name; LOW CONFIDENCE. Harmony not confirmed by name.

MP Portage pages: Luckyman is across from Rainbow Bridge via the Williwaw parking lot, Five Fingers is by Williwaw campground, Bullwinkle/Dreams of Brown Moose sit south of the visitor center high on the mountain (mountainproject.com/area/105955086/portage). Most routes are in the Williwaw side of Portage Valley; Bullwinkle pair possibly distinct. LOW CONFIDENCE, not split. Not Byron Glacier (the Byron sibling walls are rock).

MP/alaskaiceclimbing.com: Paradise Pillar (formerly Purinton Pillar) is a free-standing vertical pillar reached from the Purinton Creek bridge on the Glen Highway; no existing wall is its home. https://alaskaiceclimbing.com/paradise-pillar/

Cracked Ice is the name of the peak (MP area 117722248 and AAC report); its West Ridge (5.7 AI2-3) and Cracked Ice route are on that peak, so the area is a real place. Unknown 5.7 alpine row stays with the majority.

moves.evidence: MP: Great White Conqueror is on the North Face of the West Tower (mountainproject.com/route/106651087)

evidence: Great White Conqueror moves to the West Tower leaf. The Fall Line (M5) and West Ridge (AI1-2) could not be placed on a specific tower from sources; they stay, and the new name is descriptive only. LOW CONFIDENCE; review.
UNRESOLVED: rockclimbing.com Lake Lincoln Crags lists a 2-entry ice section but no source names the wall for Arkansas R-ice. Single route stays; a human should place or rename.
UNRESOLVED: no source found for Bedtime for Cleo. Single route stays in the leaf pending a placed name.

MP: Carson Peak Gully is the largest drainage on climbers' right of Carson Peak, and Rob's Ravine is its bottom third / the base of Pete's Dream (mountainproject.com/route/114023521/carson-peak-gully; area 114023420). All four routes are in that drainage (Guy and Dude Looks Like a Lady unconfirmed, kept with majority). Note Robs Ravine and Carson Peak Gully may be duplicates.

moves.evidence: Same Roadside Ice flow beside Hwy 158; leaf coordinates match to ~10 m (MP area 107038556)

evidence: Center section of the same Roadside Ice flow; merged into the Left Side/Main Flow leaf (which is renamed Roadside Flow).

MP area 107038556 'Roadside Ice' is one flow beside the June Lake loop road; Left Side and Center are sections of it, so a single place name is used. Receives the Center route from ca_roadside_ice_center_2.

MP: Lundy Falls (500 ft) is the main flow of Lundy Canyon Ice, and Triple Conjunction is the highest ice on the same hill, reached via the descent gully (mountainproject.com/area/111342650; route/111377684).
